transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, ah, I hope I'm not wasting your time—it's really nothing terribly dramatic, and I certainly don't want to make a fuss. 

But I came in because... well, I’ve just started to feel, in this rather quiet but stubborn way, that the best version of my life is already behind me. It feels a bit foolish to admit that out loud, honestly. I've always been a very capable, organized person, but lately it just seems like no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing people usually come here for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things properly for you.
How long have you been feeling like the best version of your life is behind you?

Well, let's see... I suppose it's been a little while now. I really hope I don't sound like I'm just complaining about getting older—I know we all have to make adjustments eventually, and I'm very fortunate in so many ways. 

But, um... I suppose it seems to have started after a hiking injury I had. Nothing too terrible, of course! But that was a little over three years ago... about three years and three months now, if I'm being precise. The injury itself healed up fine, but that sort of... flat feeling just seemed to stick around after that. 

Is that the sort of timeframe you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before the hiking injury?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've stopped enjoying things. I certainly don't want to give you the impression that I'm just sitting around the house feeling sorry for myself! I still read quite a bit, and I always look forward to seeing my family. 

I think I still find pleasure in all of that. It's just... well, I suppose I just feel a bit less vibrant while doing them, if that makes sense? But I definitely still enjoy my usual hobbies and routines. 

Does that... is that answering your question clearly enough? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right sort of information and not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you noticed any decrease in the pleasure you derive from activities that you normally find enjoyable?

Well, as I was just saying... I really wouldn't call it a decrease in pleasure, exactly. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm being clear. 

I still do all the things I've always done, and I'm very grateful for them. I certainly don't feel entirely numb to the world or anything dramatic like that. It's more of a... a subtle shift in the background, perhaps? But the enjoyment itself is still there. I really don't want to sound like I'm unappreciative of the good things in my life. 

Is that helpful? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you had any periods in the past where you felt really down or depressed for a while?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that. I mean, I've had my moments of sadness, like anyone else—losing loved ones, or when things don't quite go as planned. But never a period where I felt truly down or... or depressed for a long stretch. 

I've always been pretty good at keeping my chin up, you know? I really wouldn't want you to think I have a history of being terribly gloomy or anything. I've been very lucky to have a generally steady mood throughout my life. 

Does that sound about right? I hope I'm understanding your question correctly. I just want to be sure I'm giving you the accurate history you need.
Do you feel like you have to force yourself to participate in activities that you used to find enjoyable?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I have to *force* myself. That sounds a bit... well, a bit extreme, doesn't it? I mean, sometimes I might need a little extra cup of coffee to get going in the morning, but once I'm up and reading my paper or getting ready for a family visit, I'm perfectly happy to be doing it. 

I really try to stay active and engaged. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just dragging my feet all day. I just... maybe I just take things a little slower now, being 65 and all. But I'm still participating willingly, I promise! 

Is that what you were asking? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm a burden or that I'm completely lacking motivation. I really do try my best to keep up with everything.
Do you feel like you're having to put in more effort to enjoy the things you normally like?

Well, no... I really wouldn't call it effort. I mean, perhaps I don't jump out of my chair to get to my hobbies with the exact same vigor I did when I was thirty, but the enjoyment itself doesn't feel like work at all. 

I certainly don't want to give you the impression that my days have become chores. I still very much look forward to my usual routines. It's just... well, just a very normal, quiet sort of contentment, I suppose. I'm perfectly happy with how things are in that regard. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this well enough for your notes. I just want to be absolutely sure I'm not painting a bleaker picture than what's actually there.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Oh, no, I... I don't think so. I wouldn't say I've lost interest at all. I still very much enjoy my reading, keeping up with the news, my usual little routines. I mean, maybe I don't take on quite as many different projects as I did before I retired, but the things I do enjoy, I still care about very much. 

I certainly wouldn't want you to think I've just given up on my hobbies or that I'm just sitting around staring at the wall all day. I really do try my best to stay involved and keep my mind active. 

Are these answers okay? I know you have a lot of specific things you need to check on, and I just want to be sure I'm being helpful and giving you exactly what you need for your assessment.
How often do you feel sad or empty?

Well, I... I wouldn't use words like "sad" or "empty," really. That makes it sound so... so bleak, doesn't it? I certainly don't want to give you the impression that I'm sitting around crying all day or anything dramatic like that. I really do try to keep a positive outlook.

I suppose... if I had to describe it, it's more like... well, most days there's just this sort of low, gray tone running underneath things. Even when I'm doing something nice, like working in my studio or just sitting across from my wife at dinner. It's not a deep despair, just a... a quiet sort of flatness, I guess. 

But I manage it fine, really I do! I don't let it ruin my day or get in the way of being a good husband. I hope that doesn't sound too concerning? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture without making a mountain out of a molehill. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
How long have you been experiencing this low, gray tone running underneath things?

Well, let's see... I suppose it's been a little while now. I really don't want it to sound like I've been dragging my feet for ages, but... I think it started around the time I had that hiking injury. That would make it a little over three years ago. Maybe three years and three months, if I'm being exact? 

I know that sounds like a long time to be feeling this way, but honestly, it hasn't been unbearable. I've just sort of adapted to it, you know? Kept my chin up and carried on. I hope I should have mentioned it sooner to someone, but I really didn't want to be a bother or seem like a complainer. Does that make sense? I just try to handle things on my own as best I can.
Do you have difficulty concentrating or making decisions?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I have difficulty with those things. I mean, my concentration is perfectly fine, really. I still read my books and follow the news without any trouble at all. I certainly don't want you to think my mind is slipping or anything like that. 

As for decisions... well, I suppose I take my time with them, but I think that's just being careful, isn't it? I like to weigh my options. I don't feel like I'm paralyzed by indecision or anything dramatic. I just... I like to make sure I'm doing the right thing. 

I hope that's a helpful answer? I know you're trying to get a full picture, and I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea about how my mind is working. I'm still sharp, I promise!
Would you say this low, gray tone you described is mild, moderate, or severe?

Oh, well... I'm really not entirely sure how to measure something like that. I certainly wouldn't call it severe! Heavens, no. I really don't want to give you the impression that I'm in some sort of crisis or that I'm falling apart. 

I suppose... if I had to put a word to it, I'd say it's very mild. Just a... a faint little background noise, really. It's perfectly manageable, I assure you. I just wouldn't want to exaggerate my situation or make a fuss when there are people out there dealing with truly severe problems, you know? 

I hope it's alright that I describe it that way? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right idea without sounding like a complainer.
Do you ever find yourself feeling like you're just going through the motions of activities you used to enjoy, without really feeling any pleasure from them?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I'm just going through the motions. I mean, I still keep busy. I still tend to my garden, and I read quite a bit. I don't want it to sound like I've stopped doing things or that I'm just sitting around all day. 

I suppose... maybe the spark isn't quite as bright as it used to be? But I think that's just getting older, isn't it? Things settle down a bit. I still enjoy a nice afternoon on the porch, even if I don't get overly excited about it the way a younger man might. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I've lost all interest in life or anything drastic like that. I'm perfectly content, really. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
Do you ever feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that you used to find enjoyable?

Oh, well, I think we... we just touched on that a moment ago, didn't we? I certainly don't feel unable to experience pleasure. I wouldn't want you to think I'm incapable of enjoying my life. 

Like I mentioned, I still have my garden and my books. I still find them pleasant. It's not a... a complete loss of joy or anything terrible like that. I just think I appreciate things in a quieter way now. It's a very peaceful sort of contentment, really. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much? I just want to make sure I'm being clear that I haven't lost my ability to enjoy a nice day. I'm doing quite well in that regard, I promise.
Would you say this feeling of your life being behind you is something that bothers you a little, or something that bothers you a lot?

Oh, well... I certainly wouldn't say it bothers me a lot. That sounds a bit too dramatic, doesn't it? I'm not agonizing over it or losing sleep, I promise you. It's really just... a little bother. A mild realization, I suppose. 

But, to be perfectly honest, it is the main reason I finally decided to come in and speak with you. I've just started to feel—in a very quiet, but rather stubborn way—that the best version of my life is already behind me. And I've always been someone who could just organize and work my way out of a slump, but... lately, it just feels like no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling exactly like myself again. 

It's just a small, nagging thought, really. I hope it's alright that I share that? I don't want you to think I'm wallowing in despair or giving up on things. It's just a quiet little feeling I haven't been able to shake. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you're unable to find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, even if you're still doing them?

Oh dear, I... I feel like I must not be explaining myself very well today, and I do apologize for that. I know we've circled around this a few times now. 

I really do still find pleasure in my activities. I'm not completely numb to the world, if that's what you're worried about. I still get a lovely feeling when I'm out in the yard, or when I finish a good biography. It's just... well, as I said before, it's just a bit milder than it used to be. But I definitely still enjoy them. 

Am I perhaps misunderstanding the question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need, and I'd hate to think I'm making your job difficult by not being clear.
How many months or years have you been feeling this low, gray tone running underneath things?

Oh, well, let me think... I suppose it's been quite a while now. I hope it doesn't sound like I've just been sitting around feeling sorry for myself all this time. I really have been trying my best to manage it. 

But, if I'm being precise, I'd say it started right around the time I had a bit of a hiking injury. That was a little over three years ago... maybe three years and three months, if I'm counting correctly. 

It's just been this very subtle, quiet sort of feeling since then. Nothing I couldn't handle, of course! I just kept pushing through, trying to stay positive. Do you think it's normal for something like that to linger for a few years? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting by bringing it up after all this time.
Do you feel like you've lost the ability to feel happy or excited about things that used to bring you joy?

Oh... no, I certainly haven't lost the ability completely. Oh dear, I must really be doing a poor job of explaining myself today, and I am so sorry if I'm making us go in circles. 

I promise I haven't lost my ability to feel happy or excited. I still get a wonderful spark of excitement when I'm looking forward to a nice dinner, or when I find a new book by an author I like. It's really just... maybe the volume is turned down just a tiny fraction on those feelings, like I was trying to say earlier? But the happiness is absolutely still there. 

I really hope I'm not coming across as completely miserable or ungrateful for the good things I have. I'd hate for you to think I'm just sitting around complaining. Does that clarify things a bit better for you?
Would you describe your current feelings of flatness as something that slightly bothers you or significantly impacts your daily life?

Oh, well... I certainly wouldn't use a heavy word like "significantly." I really don't want you to think I'm falling apart or unable to cope! I still manage all the basics around the house perfectly fine, I promise. 

But... I suppose it does bother me just a little bit, mainly because... well, I have stepped back from a few things. I used to do quite a bit of mentoring, and I'd go to community events and music gatherings... and I haven't really been making any travel plans lately, either. So my weeks are just... well, they're much smaller than they used to be, if that makes sense? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or completely withdrawn. I just find it a bit easier to keep things simple right now. Does that give you the information you were looking for?
Would you describe your current feelings as mildly, moderately, or severely depressing?

Oh, um, mildly. Definitely mildly. I really hope I haven't been painting a picture of someone who's completely miserable or severely depressed. I'm certainly not in tears most days or doing anything dramatic like that. 

It's really just... well, like I mentioned before, it's just this low, gray tone running underneath everything. Even when I'm in my studio working, or just sitting across from my wife at dinner... it's just there in the background. But it's very mild, I promise. I can still function and enjoy my evenings. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right idea of how manageable it really is.
